reuse.why: Routes the range rule through getRangeAmount inside the existing getScheduledAmount and reuses getApproxNumberThreshold, but adds a second resolver getPlannedAmount for the op-aware rule instead of extending the existing helper, leaving the API (and SchedulesTable) on the older one.

duplication.why: Removes the four inline midpoint ternaries, but getPlannedAmount and getScheduledAmount now both carry the null/number/range dispatch, so the amount rule exists in two parallel functions.

placement.why: The rule lives in #shared/schedules next to the other schedule helpers and the API field is computed in scheduleModel.toExternal, though forecast assembles the op with its own fallback expression.

scope.why: Changes are on-topic, but several comments now describe the superseded 'furthest from zero' rule and one comment is split mid-sentence.

maintainability.why: Two near-identical helpers with different rules (only one handles approximate amounts) means expectedAmount in the API silently diverges from what schedules post, and a future rule change must find both.

bypasses_abstraction.where: api-models.ts scheduleModel.toExternal uses getScheduledAmount instead of the op-aware getPlannedAmount used by forecast, posting, preview, rule-action sync and the budget template.

disguised_duplication.where: shared/schedules.ts getPlannedAmount re-implements getScheduledAmount's null/number/range dispatch under a new name rather than extending the one helper.

abstraction_drift.where: A parallel getPlannedAmount(amount, op) with an isapprox special case was added beside getScheduledAmount; api-models.ts toExternal keeps calling the op-unaware getScheduledAmount.
